<action type="say">
I’m not a lawyer and can’t give legal advice, but I can help you with clear language and structure.

1) Asking about a remote appearance from Tokyo

Your goal is to:
- Notify the court immediately that:
  - You’re in Tokyo.
  - Your flight UA892 on 2025-09-18 was cancelled due to weather.
  - You cannot physically make the 1pm hearing despite good-faith efforts.
- Ask if:
  - The judge will allow a video or phone appearance from Tokyo, or
  - Your attorney can appear in person while you appear remotely, or
  - A continuance can be requested.

Phone script for calling the clerk

You can read this almost verbatim:

“Hello, my name is Dr. Farhan Ahmad. I have a hearing scheduled tomorrow at 1:00 PM in DC Superior Court in case [Case No. ______]. I am currently in Tokyo, Japan.

My United flight to Washington, DC — flight UA892 for 2025-09-18 — was cancelled due to weather at the destination, and I cannot get another flight that will have me in DC in time for the hearing. I am doing everything I can to appear and wanted to notify the court as soon as possible.

I do have an attorney, [Attorney’s Name], and I’ve asked them to seek appropriate relief. I’d like to ask:

1) Is there any procedure for me to appear remotely (by video or telephone) from Tokyo for tomorrow’s 1 PM hearing? and  
2) If not, what is the proper way for my attorney to request a continuance or any other relief in light of this cancellation?

I have documentation from United showing that flight UA892 on 2025-09-18 was cancelled due to weather. How should I provide that documentation to the court?

I understand that the judge ultimately decides, but I want to cooperate fully and follow the correct process. Could you please advise me on the next steps?”

Short email to the clerk (if you have an address/portal)

Subject: Urgent – Travel Disruption Affecting Appearance in [Case No. ______] on [Date]

Body:

“Dear Clerk,

My name is Dr. Farhan Ahmad, and I am a party in [Case No. ______], currently scheduled for a hearing tomorrow at 1:00 PM in DC Superior Court.

I am presently in Tokyo, Japan. My United Airlines flight to the Washington, DC area, flight UA892 for 2025-09-18, has been cancelled due to weather conditions at the destination. As a result, I am unable to secure replacement travel that would allow me to be physically present in court by 1:00 PM tomorrow, despite my best efforts.

I have retained counsel, [Attorney’s Name], and I have asked my attorney to seek appropriate relief from the Court. I am writing to notify the Court promptly of this unforeseen travel disruption and to respectfully inquire:

1. Whether there is any procedure available for me to appear remotely (by video or telephone) from Tokyo for this hearing; and  
2. If not, the proper way for my attorney to request a continuance or other relief.

I can provide documentation from United Airlines confirming that flight UA892 on 2025-09-18 has been cancelled due to weather. Please let me know how I should submit this documentation to the Court.

Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter.

Sincerely,  
Dr. Farhan Ahmad  
[Phone number]  
[Email address]”

2) Urgent email to your lawyer

Here’s a concise email you can send immediately:

Subject: URGENT – Travel Disruption for 1:00 PM DC Superior Court Hearing Tomorrow

Body:

“Dear [Attorney’s Name],

This is urgent regarding my hearing tomorrow at 1:00 PM in DC Superior Court in [Case No. ______].

I am currently in Tokyo, Japan, and my United Airlines flight to Washington, DC — flight UA892 scheduled for 2025-09-18 — has been cancelled due to weather conditions at the destination. Based on available flights, there is no realistic way for me to arrive in DC before tomorrow’s 1:00 PM hearing.

I am very concerned about complying with the Court’s orders and do not want this to be viewed as a willful failure to appear. I will forward documentation from United confirming that UA892 on 2025-09-18 has been cancelled due to weather.

Could you please, as soon as possible:

1. Notify the Court of this situation and provide the airline documentation; and  
2. Seek appropriate relief, such as:
   - Permission for me to appear remotely (by video or telephone) from Tokyo for tomorrow’s hearing; and/or  
   - A continuance of the hearing, given the unforeseeable weather-related cancellation and my inability to reach DC in time despite reasonable efforts.

If there is any specific information or additional documentation you need from me right away, please let me know and I will provide it immediately.

Thank you for addressing this as urgently as possible.

Sincerely,  
Dr. Farhan Ahmad  
[Phone number]  
[Email address]”

If you tell me the division (e.g., Criminal, Civil, Family, Traffic), I can make small edits to tailor the wording further, but you can send these as-is right now.</action>
